verdict.rationale: Cua's SDK creates and drives sandboxed computers on Docker/Podman (with gVisor when installed), QEMU, or Lume VMs. Its docs say coding agents can be started inside a Space or sandbox, and Cua Driver plus connectable owned machines cover the later real-device step. A hands-on user reports sandboxing Claude in a Lume VM worked reasonably well, though another early-version user hit VM connection failures. Missing for 10: a documented workflow for moving the same agent from sandbox to a real device, and more consistent hands-on reliability evidence (cua-comm-1 reports WebSocket connection failures on cua-agent 0.1.29).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent against a sandboxed VM or container before pointing it at a real device

citations.quote: the SDK uses Docker or Podman (gVisor when installed), QEMU, or Lume on Apple silicon. Any OCI image works.
Start Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents inside a Space or sandbox
Lume: macOS and Linux VMs on Apple silicon.
Cua Driver: lets an agent drive native apps on macOS, Windows and Linux in the background, through MCP or a CLI.
